questions.question: In which year was the Nobel prize awarded jointly to Eric A Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E Wieman 'for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle, and Carl E. Wieman were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in **2001**.
 
• The award was given for their groundbreaking work on the **achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC)** in dilute gases of alkali atoms.
 
• This was the first experimental realization of Bose-Einstein condensation, a state of matter predicted by **Satyendra Nath Bose** and Albert Einstein in the 1920s.
 
• Their research opened up new possibilities for exploring quantum mechanics and studying matter under extreme conditions.
 
• The Nobel Committee recognized this achievement as a significant milestone in the field of atomic physics and quantum mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC):**

 
 
• BEC is a state of matter formed when a gas of bosons is cooled to temperatures very close to absolute zero (0 Kelvin).
 
• Under such extreme conditions, a large fraction of the atoms occupy the same quantum state, forming a "superatom" with unique quantum properties.
 
 
 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose's Contribution:**
 
 
• Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose worked on the statistical mechanics of particles that obey Bose-Einstein statistics, known as bosons.
 
• Albert Einstein extended Bose's work to predict the phenomenon of BEC in the 1920s.
 
 
 
• **Experimental Setup by Nobel Laureates:**
 
 
• Cornell and Wieman used a combination of laser cooling and evaporative cooling techniques to achieve BEC in rubidium atoms in 1995.
 
• Ketterle refined the technique and demonstrated new properties of BEC, such as interference patterns between condensates.
 
 
 
• **Applications of BEC:**
 
 
• Bose-Einstein condensates are used to study quantum phenomena such as superfluidity and quantum vortices.
 
• They have potential applications in precision measurement, quantum computing, and simulations of complex quantum systems.

questions.question: In 2016, Pandit Birju Maharaj won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography for which film?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bajirao Mastani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography in 2016 for the song "**Mohe Rang Do Laal**" from the film **Bajirao Mastani**.
 
• The song features **Deepika Padukone** portraying Mastani, performing intricate Kathak moves under Pandit Birju Maharaj's choreography.
 
• This win marked a significant moment as it showcased the integration of classical Indian dance forms in mainstream Bollywood cinema.
 
• **Bajirao Mastani**, directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali, is a period drama based on the life of Peshwa Bajirao I and his love story with Mastani.
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj is a legendary Kathak dancer and choreographer, known for his contribution to preserving and modernizing the dance form globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India, originating from Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," meaning story, and "Kathakar," meaning storyteller.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures (mudras) and facial expressions.
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj is considered a doyen of the Lucknow gharana of Kathak.
 
 
 
• **Bajirao Mastani**
 
 
• Released in 2015, the film starred Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone, and Priyanka Chopra in lead roles.
 
• The movie is based on the historical romance of Maratha warrior Bajirao and his second wife Mastani.
 
• It received numerous accolades for its direction, performances, music, and choreography.
 
 
 
• **Filmfare Award for Best Choreography**
 
 
• It is an annual award presented by Filmfare as part of its Filmfare Awards for Hindi films.
 
• The award recognizes excellence in dance choreography in Bollywood films.
 
• Choreographers like Saroj Khan, Vaibhavi Merchant, and Farah Khan have won this award multiple times.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj's Contributions**
 
 
• He was born on February 4, 1938, and hailed from a family of Kathak dancers.
 
• He modernized Kathak while retaining its traditional essence, making it more accessible to global audiences.
 
• He has been honored with numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award.
 
• In addition to dance, he was also a gifted classical singer and percussionist.

questions.question: 'Disputes regarding the election of the President and Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court whose decision shall be final' is mentioned under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 71**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 71 of the Indian Constitution deals with disputes related to the election of the President and Vice-President of India.
 
• It states that such disputes shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision shall be final and binding.
 
• The Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over these election-related matters, ensuring neutrality and fairness in the resolution process.
 
• This article ensures that the highest judicial authority in the country addresses any irregularities or legal issues in the election process.
 
• Article 71 also emphasizes that no election of a President or Vice-President can be called into question on the ground of any vacancy or defect in the electoral college.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 54:** This article specifies the composition of the electoral college responsible for electing the President of India, which includes elected members of the Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• **Article 58:** It lays down the qualifications required for a person to be eligible for election as the President of India, such as citizenship, age, and eligibility to become a Member of Parliament.
 
• **Article 74:** This article mentions the role of the Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, in aiding and advising the President in the exercise of their functions.
 
• **Supreme Court's Role:** The Supreme Court acts as the ultimate authority to resolve disputes under Article 71, ensuring that the constitutional process of electing the President and Vice-President is upheld.
 
• **Election Commission:** While the Election Commission conducts elections for the President and Vice-President, disputes arising from such elections fall under the purview of Article 71, giving the Supreme Court the final decision-making authority.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities introduced the Sattriya dance in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Srimanta Sankardev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Srimanta Sankardev** was a 15th–16th century saint-reformer, scholar, and cultural icon of Assam.
 
• He introduced the **Sattriya dance** as a medium of propagating Vaishnavism and devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• Sattriya dance is one of the **eight classical dance forms of India**, recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
 
• The dance form originated in **Sattras** (Vaishnavite monasteries) established by Srimanta Sankardev in Assam.
 
• Sattriya incorporates **mythological themes** and is performed as an expression of devotion through storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srimanta Sankardev's Contribution:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Ekasarana Dharma**, a neo-Vaishnavite religious movement in Assam.
 
• Sankardev composed **Borgeets** (devotional songs), **Ankiya Nat** (one-act plays), and other literary works to promote Bhakti.
 
• His teachings emphasized the unity of humanity, rejecting caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Characteristics:**
 
 
• It integrates elements of **nritta** (pure dance), **nritya** (expressive dance), and **natya** (dramatic storytelling).
 
• The dance is performed in traditional Assamese attire, such as the **Paat silk**.
 
• The accompanying music includes khol (drum), cymbals, and chanting of scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Sattras:**
 
 
• Sattras are Vaishnavite monasteries established by Srimanta Sankardev and his disciples.
 
• They served as centers for the practice of religion, culture, and education.
 
• Sattras continue to play a significant role in preserving Assamese culture and the Sattriya dance tradition.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Sattriya Dance:**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized Sattriya as a classical dance form of India in **2000**.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to promote and preserve the dance form globally.

questions.question: As per National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023, how many indicators were included while calculating multidimensional poverty in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023, developed by NITI Aayog, includes **12 indicators** across three key dimensions: health, education, and standard of living.
 
• The MPI measures poverty by assessing deprivation in multiple aspects of life beyond just income levels.
 
• The 12 indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, and bank accounts.
 
• It is part of India's efforts to align with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), specifically Goal 1: "No Poverty."
 
• The National MPI leverages data from reliable sources like the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) and other government data sets for accurate calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It uses indicators that reflect different aspects of poverty beyond monetary measures.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• A global framework adopted by all UN member states in 2015 to achieve a better and more sustainable future by 2030.
 
• Goal 1 ("No Poverty") seeks to eradicate poverty in all its forms, including multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS):**
 
 
• A large-scale, multi-round survey conducted in a representative sample of households throughout India.
 
• Provides essential data on health, nutrition, and standard of living indicators for MPI calculations.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions of MPI:**
 
 
• Health: Includes indicators like nutrition and child mortality.
 
• Education: Includes years of schooling and school attendance.
 
• Standard of Living: Includes access to cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.

questions.question: Which football club in India has the longest history?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarada FC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sarada FC**, founded in 1879, is the oldest football club in India and among the oldest in Asia.
 
• The club was established in Calcutta (now Kolkata), which was the hub of football during British colonial rule in India.
 
• Sarada FC is considered a pioneer in introducing organized football in India and has a significant historical legacy.
 
• Although the club is not active in modern professional football, its contribution to the foundation of Indian football remains notable.
 
• The early emergence of clubs like Sarada FC helped popularize football as a sport in India, particularly in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Football in India:**

 
 
• Football was introduced in India by British soldiers and gained popularity in the late 19th century.
 
• Calcutta became the epicenter of Indian football, with several clubs emerging during British rule.
 
• The Durand Cup, established in 1888, is one of the oldest football tournaments globally and is still held annually in India.
 
 
 
• **East Bengal Club:**
 
 
• Founded in 1920, East Bengal Club is one of India’s most famous football clubs, with a rich legacy in both domestic and international tournaments.
 
• It is part of the historic Kolkata football rivalry with Mohun Bagan, known as the "Boro Match" or "Kolkata Derby."
 
 
 
• **Mohun Bagan Athletic Club:**
 
 
• Founded in 1889, Mohun Bagan is another iconic football club in India, known for its historic victory against the East Yorkshire Regiment in 1911.
 
• That victory marked the first time an Indian team defeated a British team, symbolizing national pride.
 
 
 
• **Indian Super League (ISL):**
 
 
• Launched in 2014, the ISL is a professional football league in India aimed at increasing the popularity of football nationwide.
 
• Clubs like Mumbai City FC and ATK Mohun Bagan are prominent participants in the league.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Football in Bengal:**
 
 
• Bengal has been the heart of Indian football for over a century, producing many legendary players and hosting iconic matches.
 
• The passion for football in Bengal remains strong, with clubs like East Bengal and Mohun Bagan enjoying massive fan followings.

questions.question: During which Five-Year Plan (FYP) was the Department of Biotechnology set up by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) was established by the Government of India in **1986**, during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990)**.
 
• It was created to promote and develop biotechnology research and applications in India, focusing on various fields such as agriculture, healthcare, environment, and industrial processes.
 
• The DBT operates under the Ministry of Science and Technology, supporting innovation and scientific advancements.
 
• It has been instrumental in fostering public-private partnerships and promoting research institutes to advance biotechnology in India.
 
• The establishment of DBT marked a significant step towards strengthening India's scientific infrastructure and biotechnology sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans (FYP):**

 
 
• India adopted Five-Year Plans post-independence, modeled after the Soviet Union, to organize its economic and developmental strategies.
 
• The Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990) focused on modernization, technological development, and improving productivity in various sectors.
 
• It emphasized self-reliance and the development of industries such as biotechnology, energy, and telecommunications.
 
 
 
• **Biotechnology:**
 
 
• Biotechnology is the use of biological systems, organisms, or derivatives to develop products and technologies for various applications.
 
• It plays a vital role in healthcare, agriculture, environmental conservation, and industrial processes.
 
• Key areas include genetic engineering, biopharmaceuticals, bioinformatics, and enzyme technology.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of DBT:**
 
 
• DBT has launched numerous initiatives like the National Biopharma Mission and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC).
 
• It supports biotechnology parks, research institutes, and skill development programs to boost innovation in the sector.
 
• It has been pivotal in vaccine development, genome research, and environmental biotechnology projects.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Science and Technology:**
 
 
• Established in 1971, this ministry oversees scientific research and innovation in India.
 
• It includes three departments: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR).
 
• The ministry fosters collaboration between academia, industry, and research institutions for technological growth.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are listed under which Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 36-51**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India, spanning **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• DPSPs are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, aimed at achieving socio-economic justice and promoting the welfare of the people.
 
• These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but are considered fundamental in governance.
 
• Key objectives under DPSPs include ensuring equitable distribution of wealth, reducing inequality, and improving living standards.
 
• The concept of DPSPs was borrowed from the Irish Constitution and reflects the ideals of a welfare state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Categories of DPSPs:**

 
 
• **Social and Economic Principles:** Articles like 38, 39, and 41 focus on equitable distribution of resources and providing social security to citizens.
 
• **Gandhian Principles:** Articles such as 40 emphasize the organization of village panchayats and promotion of cottage industries.
 
• **Liberal Intellectual Principles:** Articles like 44 advocate for a Uniform Civil Code and promotion of international peace (Article 51).
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature:** Although DPSPs are not enforceable in courts, they serve as a moral guide for lawmakers and policymakers.
 
• **Relation to Fundamental Rights:** DPSPs complement Fundamental Rights by addressing areas such as socio-economic welfare, while Fundamental Rights focus on civil liberties.
 
• **Key Amendments:** The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added provisions such as Article 39A for free legal aid and Article 43A for worker participation in management.
 
• **Implementation Examples:** Initiatives like the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) are inspired by DPSP principles.

questions.question: Which king of the Maukharis claimed to have defeated the Later Guptas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarvavarman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sarvavarman** was a ruler of the Maukhari dynasty, which emerged as a prominent power in North India during the 6th century CE.
 
• He is known for claiming victory over the **Later Guptas**, a dynasty that ruled Magadha after the decline of the Gupta Empire.
 
• The Maukhari dynasty, under Sarvavarman, expanded its territory, asserting its dominance in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab region.
 
• Sarvavarman's victory over the Later Guptas is documented in historical inscriptions, showcasing the rivalry between the Maukharis and the Later Guptas during this period.
 
• The success of Sarvavarman marked the decline of the Later Guptas and the rise of the Maukhari dynasty as a significant political power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maukhari Dynasty**

 
 
• The Maukhari dynasty initially served as vassals under the Guptas but later became independent rulers in the 6th century CE.
 
• Their capital was at **Kannauj**, which emerged as a key political and cultural center during their reign.
 
• The dynasty is known for its contributions to temple architecture and inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Later Guptas**
 
 
• The Later Guptas ruled Magadha and neighboring regions after the decline of the Gupta Empire.
 
• They faced continuous challenges from emerging regional powers like the Maukharis and the Vardhanas.
 
• Their fall marked the fragmentation of North India into smaller kingdoms and the end of the classical Gupta age.
 
 
 
• **Kannauj**
 
 
• Kannauj became a significant center of power under the Maukhari dynasty and later under rulers like Harsha.
 
• It was strategically located on the trade routes connecting North India to other regions.
 
• Over the centuries, Kannauj witnessed several power struggles due to its prime location and resources.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The 6th century CE was a transitional period in Indian history, marked by the decline of the Gupta Empire and the rise of regional powers like the Maukharis, Vardhanas, and others.
 
• This era saw significant political, cultural, and economic developments, with the rise of new urban centers and trade networks.
 
• Inscriptions and coins from this period are key sources of information about the rulers and their achievements.

questions.question: In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1942**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cripps Mission was sent to India in **March 1942** during World War II.
 
• It was led by Sir Stafford Cripps, a senior British politician and member of the War Cabinet.
 
• The mission aimed to secure Indian cooperation in the British war effort by offering a framework for **Indian self-government after the war**.
 
• The proposal included dominion status for India and the option for provinces to opt out of the Indian union.
 
• The Cripps Mission failed as it was rejected by both the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dominion Status:**

 
 
• Dominion status refers to a semi-independent political status under the British Crown.
 
• It was proposed for India, allowing self-rule while remaining part of the British Commonwealth.
 
 
 
• **World War II and India:**
 
 
• India was forced into World War II by Britain without consulting Indian leaders.
 
• This decision led to widespread resentment and demands for independence.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress Reaction:**
 
 
• The Congress rejected the Cripps proposals, demanding complete independence instead of dominion status.
 
• They were also opposed to the idea of provinces having the option to secede.
 
 
 
• **Muslim League Reaction:**
 
 
• The Muslim League opposed the Cripps Mission, as it did not sufficiently address their demand for a separate state (Pakistan).
 
 
 
• **Impact of Failure:**
 
 
• The failure of the Cripps Mission led to increased tensions and the launch of the **Quit India Movement** by the Congress in August 1942.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, in which State is the difference in male and female literacy rates the lowest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Census 2011, Kerala recorded the **lowest difference in male and female literacy rates**, showcasing its progressive approach toward gender equality in education.
 
• The literacy rate in Kerala was **94% for males** and **92% for females**, with a minimal gender gap of just 2 percentage points.
 
• Kerala has consistently maintained its position as the **state with the highest overall literacy rate** in India, at 93.91% as per Census 2011.
 
• Government initiatives such as **"Kerala State Literacy Mission"** and investments in education have played a crucial role in achieving this milestone.
 
• Kerala's emphasis on female literacy and empowerment has contributed significantly to its overall socio-economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate Definition:** The literacy rate is calculated as the percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• **Gender Gap in Literacy:** The gender gap is the difference in literacy rates between males and females, highlighting disparities in access to education.
 
• **Census 2011 Highlights:**
 
 
• India's overall literacy rate was 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
 
• Kerala was the most literate state, while Bihar had the lowest literacy rate at 61.8%.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Education Model:**
 
 
• Kerala's education system is characterized by universal education, high enrollment rates, and a focus on inclusive schooling.
 
• Programs such as "Akshara Kerala" and strong public school networks contribute to its educational success.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Literacy on Development:** Higher literacy rates, especially among women, are linked to improved health outcomes, lower fertility rates, and enhanced economic participation.

questions.question: In economics, which of the following concepts is defined over a period of time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Flow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Flow variables** are defined over a period of time. Examples include income, expenditure, GDP, and savings.
 
• A flow variable measures changes or activity during a specific duration, such as a month, quarter, or year.
 
• Flows are essential for understanding economic dynamics, such as production, consumption, and investment trends.
 
• Unlike stock variables, flow variables cannot be measured at a single point in time; they require a time interval for evaluation.
 
• Key examples of flow variables in economics include government budget deficits, export revenues, and investment inflows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stock Variables:**

 
 
• Stock variables are measured at a specific point in time, such as wealth, capital, or population.
 
• They represent the accumulated quantity or level of a resource at a given moment.
 
• Key examples include foreign exchange reserves, inventory levels, and national debt.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Stock and Flow:**
 
 
• Flow variables are dynamic and change over time, while stock variables are static and represent a snapshot.
 
• Flow impacts stock, e.g., savings (flow) increase wealth (stock).
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):**
 
 
• GDP is a flow variable representing the total economic output of a country over a specific time period.
 
• It is typically measured quarterly or annually and includes components like consumption, investment, and government spending.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP):**
 
 
• BoP records all financial flows into and out of a country during a specific time period.
 
• It includes current account, capital account, and financial account transactions.

questions.question: Who among the following singers had been conferred with the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award of India, in 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishnan Nair Shantakumari Chithra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Krishnan Nair Shantakumari Chithra, popularly known as **K.S. Chithra**, is an acclaimed playback singer from Kerala, India.
 
• She was conferred with the **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian award, in 2021 for her outstanding contribution to Indian music.
 
• Chithra has won multiple awards, including **6 National Film Awards**, 8 Filmfare Awards South, and numerous state awards for her playback singing.
 
• She is widely regarded as one of the **greatest playback singers** in Indian cinema, with recordings in over 20 languages.
 
• Known as the "Melody Queen," she has sung over **25,000 songs** in her illustrious career, spanning several decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are among the **highest civilian honors** in India and are announced annually on Republic Day.
 
• They are classified into three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (highest), **Padma Bhushan** (second-highest), and **Padma Shri** (third-highest).
 
• The awards recognize exceptional contributions in various fields, including art, literature, science, sports, social work, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Playback Singing in India:**
 
 
• Playback singing is a unique feature of Indian cinema where singers record songs that actors lip-sync during filming.
 
• The industry has produced legendary singers like **Lata Mangeshkar**, **Kishore Kumar**, **Mohammed Rafi**, and **Asha Bhosle**.
 
• These songs often become chartbusters and contribute significantly to the popularity of films.
 
 
 
• **K.S. Chithra's Legacy:**
 
 
• Chithra is known for her versatile voice and ability to sing classical, devotional, and contemporary songs with equal finesse.
 
• She holds the distinction of being the **first Indian woman** to perform at the United Nations General Assembly.
 
• Her contributions to music have earned her global recognition, including prestigious awards and honors.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate from the peninsular plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Gandak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Gandak River** does not originate from the peninsular plateau; it originates from the **Nepal Himalayas**.
 
• The Gandak flows through Nepal and enters India in Bihar, where it merges with the Ganges.
 
• The river is formed by the confluence of several Himalayan streams, including **Kali Gandaki** and **Trishuli.**
 
• Unlike rivers such as the Son, Chambal, and Mahanadi, which originate from the peninsular plateau, the Gandak belongs to the category of Himalayan rivers.
 
• The Gandak basin supports a rich ecosystem and is known for its fertile plains, contributing significantly to agriculture in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau Rivers:**

 
 
• Rivers such as the Chambal, Son, Mahanadi, and Godavari originate from the peninsular plateau of India.
 
• These rivers are typically non-glacial and rely on rainfall for their flow.
 
• They exhibit seasonal flow patterns, with high water levels during the monsoon and reduced flow during dry periods.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• Rivers like the Gandak, Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus originate from the Himalayan mountain range.
 
• These rivers are glacial-fed and perennial, ensuring continuous flow throughout the year.
 
• They play a crucial role in sustaining agriculture and supporting livelihoods across northern India.
 
 
 
• **The Ganges River System:**
 
 
• The Gandak River is an important tributary of the Ganges river system.
 
• Other major tributaries include the Yamuna, Ghaghara, Kosi, and Son rivers.
 
• The Ganges basin is one of the most fertile and densely populated regions in the world.
 
 
 
• **River Classification in India:**
 
 
• Indian rivers are broadly classified as Himalayan rivers and Peninsular rivers.
 
• Himalayan rivers are perennial, while peninsular rivers are generally seasonal.
 
• The classification is based on their origin, flow characteristics, and dependence on rainfall or glacial melt.

questions.question: All the five-year plans were not given equal importance due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limitation of Resources**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• All five-year plans in India were designed to achieve specific developmental goals, but their implementation faced challenges due to **limited availability of resources**, such as financial, natural, and human resources.
 
• The government had to prioritize sectors and allocate resources accordingly, leading to unequal emphasis across various plans.
 
• The scarcity of resources was more pronounced in the initial five-year plans, as India was a newly independent country with a weak industrial base and low economic growth.
 
• The focus areas of each plan, such as agriculture, industry, or infrastructure, were determined based on the **resource constraints** and the immediate needs of the nation.
 
• Resource constraints were further exacerbated by factors such as population growth, external conflicts, and natural calamities, affecting the uniform implementation of the plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India's five-year plans were initiated in 1951, inspired by the Soviet model of planned economic development.
 
• The **Planning Commission** was responsible for formulating and monitoring the plans until its replacement by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture, while subsequent plans diversified into industrialization, technology, and social welfare.
 
 
 
• **Resource Constraints**
 
 
• Resource constraints refer to the limited availability of essential inputs like funds, manpower, raw materials, and infrastructure.
 
• These limitations force governments to prioritize and allocate resources selectively, often at the expense of other sectors.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Resource Scarcity**
 
 
• Uneven development across different regions and sectors.
 
• Inability to achieve long-term goals due to short-term compromises in resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **Shift to NITI Aayog**
 
 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog**, focusing on a more decentralized and participatory planning approach.
 
• NITI Aayog emphasizes cooperative federalism and long-term policy strategies, addressing resource constraints more efficiently.

questions.question: What is the name of the Indian Kho-Kho league tournament/event in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultimate Kho-Kho**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ultimate Kho-Kho** is India’s first professional Kho-Kho league, launched to promote the traditional Indian sport on a larger scale.
 
• The inaugural season of Ultimate Kho-Kho took place in **August 2022**, featuring six franchise teams.
 
• The league is organized under the aegis of the **Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI)** and is backed by Dabur Group chairman Amit Burman as its promoter.
 
• Ultimate Kho-Kho follows a unique format with exciting innovations such as **power plays** and **dynamic scoring rules** to make the game more engaging for spectators.
 
• The league aims to increase the global appeal of Kho-Kho while nurturing and showcasing Indian talent in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kho-Kho**

 
 
• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag sport that dates back to ancient times and is widely played across the country.
 
• The game involves two teams of 12 players each, with nine players on the field at a time.
 
• It requires agility, speed, strategy, and teamwork to chase and tag opponents within a fixed time frame.
 
 
 
• **Innovations in Ultimate Kho-Kho**
 
 
• The league introduced concepts like **Wazir** (a key player with special powers) and **power play** to make the game fast-paced and strategically challenging.
 
• Dynamic scoring rules reward teams for tagging multiple players in quick succession, adding excitement to the matches.
 
 
 
• **Kho-Kho Federation of India (KKFI)**
 
 
• KKFI is the governing body responsible for promoting and regulating Kho-Kho in India.
 
• It is affiliated with the **Asian Kho Kho Federation** and the **International Kho Kho Federation**, working to expand the sport globally.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ultimate Kho-Kho**
 
 
• The league has provided a platform for grassroots players to showcase their talent on a national stage.
 
• It has also attracted corporate sponsorships and broadcast partnerships, enhancing the sport's visibility and popularity.

questions.question: Who gave the keynote address at the Conference on Maritime Decarbonization in India, which was held on October 3, 2024 in New Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TK Ramachandran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• TK Ramachandran, Chairman of the Visakhapatnam Port Authority, delivered the keynote address at the Conference on Maritime Decarbonization in India.
 
• The conference was held on **October 3, 2024, in New Delhi**, focusing on strategies for reducing carbon emissions in the maritime sector.
 
• Ramachandran emphasized the importance of adopting **green shipping practices** to achieve India’s decarbonization goals under the Paris Agreement.
 
• He also highlighted the role of technology and alternative fuels in transforming the maritime industry toward sustainability.
 
• The event was attended by key stakeholders, including policymakers, industry leaders, and environmentalists, underscoring India's commitment to achieving net-zero emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maritime Decarbonization:**

 
 
• It refers to reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the maritime sector, which accounts for approximately 2.89% of global CO₂ emissions.
 
• Technological advancements like energy-efficient ship designs, renewable energy integration, and wind-assisted propulsion are critical for decarbonization.
 
• Alternative fuels such as green hydrogen, ammonia, and biofuels are being explored as replacements for conventional marine fuels.
 
 
 
• **India’s Maritime Vision 2030:**
 
 
• A comprehensive plan to develop sustainable and globally competitive ports in India.
 
• Focuses on **green port initiatives**, digitization, and the adoption of clean energy solutions in the maritime sector.
 
 
 
• **International Maritime Organization (IMO) Regulations:**
 
 
• The IMO has set targets to reduce carbon emissions from international shipping by at least 40% by 2030 and 70% by 2050 compared to 2008 levels.
 
• Key IMO strategies include the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) and Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP).
 
 
 
• **Green Shipping Corridors:**
 
 
• These are defined shipping routes where vessels operate using zero-emission fuels.
 
• Several countries, including India, are working toward establishing such corridors to promote sustainable trade.

questions.question: The saliva helps in the digestion of food in animals. What does it do?

options.text: Prevents food from entering the wind pipe
Helps is sensing taste of food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breaks down starch into sugar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saliva contains an enzyme called **salivary amylase** (also known as ptyalin) which breaks down starch into simpler sugars like maltose and dextrin.
 
• This enzymatic action begins in the mouth, marking the **first step of carbohydrate digestion**.
 
• Saliva moistens food, forming a bolus, which facilitates easier swallowing and transportation through the esophagus.
 
• The digestion process initiated by saliva is temporary and is halted when food reaches the stomach due to the acidic environment.
 
• Saliva also contains water, mucin, and electrolytes, supporting its digestive and lubricating functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salivary Glands**

 
 
• There are three main types of salivary glands: **parotid, submandibular, and sublingual glands**, which secrete saliva into the oral cavity.
 
• The parotid gland is the largest and primarily produces watery saliva rich in enzymes.
 
• Submandibular and sublingual glands produce a mix of serous (enzyme-rich) and mucous (lubricating) secretions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Saliva in Oral Health**
 
 
• Saliva contains antimicrobial agents like lysozyme that help protect the oral cavity from infections.
 
• It maintains the pH balance in the mouth, preventing tooth decay caused by acids.
 
• Saliva also aids in cleansing the mouth by washing away food particles and debris.
 
 
 
• **Enzymatic Action of Salivary Amylase**
 
 
• Salivary amylase hydrolyzes α-1,4 glycosidic bonds in starch, resulting in simpler sugars.
 
• The optimal pH for salivary amylase activity is between **6.7 and 7.0**, which matches the neutral pH of saliva.
 
 
 
• **Other Functions of Saliva**
 
 
• Saliva facilitates tasting by dissolving food molecules, allowing them to interact with taste buds.
 
• It lubricates and softens food, making it easier to chew and swallow.
 
• Saliva also plays a role in maintaining speech clarity and oral tissue hydration.

questions.question: How many national festivals are celebrated in India as of 01 January 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India celebrates three main national festivals: **Republic Day (January 26), Independence Day (August 15), and Gandhi Jayanti (October 2)**.
 
• **Republic Day** honors the adoption of the Indian Constitution on January 26, 1950, making India a republic.
 
• **Independence Day** marks the country's freedom from British rule on August 15, 1947.
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti** commemorates the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, on October 2.
 
• These festivals are observed nationwide with official ceremonies and cultural activities, reflecting India's unity and patriotic spirit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Republic Day**

 
 
• It celebrates the implementation of the Indian Constitution, replacing the Government of India Act 1935.
 
• The main celebration occurs in New Delhi, with a grand parade showcasing India's cultural diversity and military strength.
 
 
 
• **Independence Day**
 
 
• On this day, the Prime Minister hoists the National Flag at the Red Fort in New Delhi and delivers a speech to the nation.
 
• It is a day of remembrance for freedom fighters and their sacrifices for India's independence.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti**
 
 
• It is a national holiday dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi's principles of non-violence (Ahimsa) and truth (Satya).
 
• The day is marked by prayer services, tributes, and cultural events across the country.
 
 
 
• **National Significance**
 
 
• These festivals are distinct from religious or regional celebrations, as they are recognized across all states and communities of India.
 
• They reinforce India's identity as a secular, democratic, and diverse nation.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in India on August 1, 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Preeti Sudan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Preeti Sudan was appointed as the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on **August 1, 2024**.
 
• She is a retired IAS officer from the **Andhra Pradesh cadre (1983 batch)** with extensive administrative experience.
 
• Preeti Sudan has previously served as the **Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, where she played a pivotal role during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• She succeeded Dr. Manoj Soni, who served as the Chairperson of UPSC prior to her appointment.
 
• The UPSC is India's premier recruitment agency for All India Services and Central Civil Services, ensuring a fair and merit-based selection process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

 
 
• The UPSC is a constitutional body established under **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It conducts examinations for recruitment to services such as IAS, IPS, IFS, and other Group A and Group B posts.
 
• The commission operates independently and reports directly to the President of India.
 
 
 
• **Preeti Sudan’s Contributions**
 
 
• As Health Secretary, she led critical initiatives like the **Ayushman Bharat Scheme** and India's response to COVID-19.
 
• She was instrumental in policy-making for public health, sanitation, and nutrition improvement.
 
 
 
• **Role of UPSC Chairperson**
 
 
• The Chairperson is responsible for supervising the commission’s operations, including conducting exams and interviews.
 
• The Chairperson serves for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **UPSC Members**
 
 
• The UPSC consists of a Chairperson and up to 10 other members, as per the President's discretion.
 
• Members are chosen based on their expertise in public service, administration, or academia.
